tools.name: zen_of_ansible
tools.description: 20 aphorisms that describe Ansible's design philosophy.

tools.name: ansible_content_best_practices
tools.description:
Get best practices and guidelines for writing Ansible content. This tool returns relevant guidelines based on the topic you ask about. 

**How to use:** 
- Call with no topic to see available topics - Call with a specific topic to get detailed guidelines for that area 

**Examples:** 
- `{}` → Returns list of available topics - `{"topic": "yaml formatting"}` → Returns YAML formatting guidelines - `{"topic": "naming conventions"}` → Returns naming convention rules - `{"topic": "roles"}` → Returns role structure and best practices - `{"topic": "playbooks"}` → Returns playbook guidelines 

Available topics include: Guiding Principles, Development Workflow, Coding Standards, Formatting, Naming Conventions, Collections, Roles, Inventories, Variables, Playbooks, Jinja2 Templates, and more.

topic.description: The topic to get guidelines for (e.g., 'yaml formatting', 'naming conventions', 'roles', 'playbooks'). Leave empty to see all available topics.

tools.name: list_available_tools
tools.description: Shows all available Ansible Development Tools MCP Server tools. Use this to discover what tools you can use. Perfect for exploring capabilities and finding the right tool for your task.

tools.name: ansible_lint
tools.description:
**PREFERRED APPROACH**: Instead of using this MCP tool, use terminal commands to run ansible-lint. Execute commands like: `ansible-lint playbooks/deploy.yml` or `ansible-lint site.yml --fix`. The LLM can infer the file path from the currently open file, files mentioned in conversation, or workspace context. This approach works better because the LLM naturally understands file paths in terminal commands. 

**Alternative (if terminal is not available)**: This tool can run ansible-lint programmatically, but requires the `filePath` parameter. The tool will attempt auto-detection if filePath is not provided, but using terminal commands is the recommended approach.

filePath.description: Path to the Ansible playbook file to lint. **Note**: Using terminal commands (e.g., 'ansible-lint playbooks/deploy.yml') is preferred. This parameter is only needed if using the MCP tool directly.

fix.description: Whether to apply automatic fixes using ansible-lint --fix. If not specified, tool will prompt user for preference.

tools.name: ansible_navigator

filePath.description: Advanced: Direct file path to the playbook. If provided, this takes precedence over userMessage parsing. Most of the time, just use userMessage instead.

mode.description: Output mode: 'stdout' (default for this tool, direct terminal output) or 'interactive' (TUI for exploration). Only specify if user explicitly requests a different mode.

environment.description: Environment selection: 'auto' (default, checks PATH first, then venv), 'system' (only use PATH/system), 'venv' (only use virtual environment), or a specific venv name/path (e.g., 'ansible-dev', 'venv', '/path/to/venv'). When a specific venv name is provided, the tool searches in the workspace and parent directories.

disableExecutionEnvironment.description: Set to `true` to disable execution environments (passes --ee false). **Use this if you encounter Podman/Docker errors.** When disabled, ansible-navigator will use the local Ansible installation instead of containerized execution environments.

tools.name: ade_environment_info
tools.description: Get comprehensive environment information including Python, Ansible, ADE, ADT status, and installed collections. Use this tool when you need to check environment status, verify installations, inspect versions, or troubleshoot missing dependencies.

tools.name: ade_setup_environment
tools.description:
Set up a complete Ansible development environment with OS-aware package manager detection. 

**IMPORTANT:** You MUST provide `osType` and `osDistro` parameters. If the user hasn't specified their OS, ASK THEM before calling this tool.

**Package Manager Mapping:**
- Fedora/RHEL/CentOS → `dnf`
- Ubuntu/Debian → `apt`
- macOS → `brew`
- Arch → `pacman`


CRITICAL: For Ansible collections (amazon.aws, ansible.posix, etc.), you MUST use the 'collections' parameter. DO NOT put collection names in 'requirementsFile' - that is ONLY for pip packages. Correct: {collections: ['amazon.aws', 'ansible.posix']}. Wrong: {requirementsFile: 'amazon.aws'}.

envName.description: Name for the virtual environment directory (default: 'venv')

pythonVersion.description: Python version to use (e.g., '3.11', '3.12'). Will auto-install if not available.

collections.description: Ansible collections to install via ansible-galaxy. Examples: ['amazon.aws', 'ansible.posix', 'community.general']. Use this for any collection names like namespace.collection format.

installRequirements.description: Set to true to install Python packages from requirements.txt

requirementsFile.description: Path to pip requirements.txt file ONLY. NOT for Ansible collections! For collections like amazon.aws, use the 'collections' parameter instead.

osType.description: **REQUIRED** - Operating system type: 'linux' or 'darwin' (macOS). ASK THE USER if not known.

osDistro.description: **REQUIRED for Linux** - OS distribution name. Maps to package manager: 'fedora'→dnf, 'ubuntu'→apt, 'macos'→brew. ASK THE USER if not known.

tools.name: adt_check_env
tools.description: Check if ADT (ansible-dev-tools) is installed and install it if missing. ADT provides essential Ansible development tools including ansible-lint, ansible-navigator, and ansible-builder. Use this tool to ensure your Ansible development environment has all the necessary tools configured.

tools.name: create_ansible_projects
tools.description: Create new Ansible collection or playbook project using ansible-creator. This tool supports both collection and playbook project types with an interactive flow. If project type is not specified, the tool will prompt you to choose between collection or playbook. Then it will guide you through providing the required information (collection name, path, etc.). Use this tool to scaffold new Ansible projects with proper structure and best practices.

projectType.description: The type of project to create: 'collection' for Ansible collections or 'playbook' for playbook projects. If not provided, the tool will prompt you to specify this first.

namespace.description: The collection namespace (e.g., 'test_org'). Required for both collection and playbook projects. Must be provided along with 'collectionName'.

collectionName.description: The collection name (e.g., 'test_coll'). Required for both collection and playbook projects. For playbook projects, this is the name of the adjacent collection. Must be provided along with 'namespace'. The full collection name will be constructed as 'namespace.collectionName'.

projectDirectory.description: The name of the project directory where the project will be created (e.g., 'my_playbook_proj', 'my_collection_proj'). The directory will be created inside the workspace. If not provided, the tool will prompt you to specify this.

path.description: Advanced: Full destination directory path for the project. If provided, this takes precedence over projectDirectory. For collections, the collection will be created at <path>/ansible_collections/<namespace>/<collectionName>. For playbooks, the project will be created at the specified path.

tools.name: define_and_build_execution_env
tools.description: Create an EE definition file for building Ansible execution environment images with ansible-builder. This tool works in two steps: (1) First call returns a prompt with rules and requirements - generate YAML from this prompt. (2) Second call with the 'generatedYaml' parameter containing the YAML content will create and validate the file. Use rules from ee-rules.md and validate against the execution environment schema.

baseImage.description: The base container image to use (e.g., 'quay.io/fedora/fedora-minimal:41' or 'quay.io/centos/centos:stream10')

tag.description: The tag/name for the resulting execution environment image (e.g., 'my-ee:latest')

destinationPath.description: Optional destination directory path for the execution-environment.yml file. Defaults to workspace root.

collections.description: Optional array of Ansible collection names to include (e.g., ['amazon.aws', 'ansible.utils'])

systemPackages.description: Optional array of system packages to install (e.g., ['git', 'vim', 'curl'])

pythonPackages.description: Optional array of Python packages to install (e.g., ['boto3', 'requests'])

generatedYaml.description: Internal parameter: LLM-generated YAML content. Use this when calling the tool a second time after generating the YAML from the prompt provided in the first call.
